fullAnalysis: If you found yourself scratching your head over Pinpoint #528, you're in good company. Today's clues – YEAR, GUIDE, SKETCH, REFERENCE, and COFFEE-TABLE – felt like a scattered collection at first glance. But don't worry, the path to finding today's answer is clearer than you might think.

I started out pretty confident when I saw the first clue, YEAR. "YearBOOK," I thought immediately. I typed in BOOK and waited for the fireworks. Nothing. Big mistake. YEARBOOK seemed like such a solid connection, so I was completely stumped.

Then GUIDE popped up, and I was even more confused. How could YEAR and GUIDE possibly connect to the same word? I tried some random guesses like JOURNAL, but that obviously didn't work either. Total confusion.

Finally, the lightbulb went off when I saw COFFEE-TABLE. A COFFEE-TABLE book! And suddenly, the other clues fell into place. REFERENCE book, YEAR book, GUIDE book, SKETCH book. The answer was BOOKS!
Pinpoint tested not just vocabulary but also associative thinking. The clues required you to think beyond the obvious and consider broader categories.
Overall, this Pinpoint puzzle required a bit of lateral thinking. Once you realized the common theme, though, it became much easier to solve.

wordHints.Year: Yearbook is a book containing photos and memories from a particular year.
wordHints.Guide: Guidebook matches perfectly with those books for tourists or travelers.
wordHints.Sketch: Referring to a sketchbook, which is a book of blank pages for sketching.
wordHints.Reference: A nod to a reference book, used for looking up information.
wordHints.Coffee-table: Matches perfectly with coffee table book, a large, visually appealing book.

lessons.title: "Year" and "Guide" set the useful boundary
lessons.body: It's tempting to latch onto the first word that comes to mind, but today's Pinpoint proves that's a trap. I was so sure YEAR meant 'YEARBOOK' that I ignored the other clues for too long.

lessons.title: "Coffee-table" is the clue to retest before committing
lessons.body: Sometimes the connection isn't a direct compound word but a shared category. All the clues were types of BOOKS.

lessons.title: "Sketch" keeps the category level specific
lessons.body: When you're stuck, try looking at the clues from a different angle. Instead of thinking about individual words, think about what they have in common.

lessons: Use the clues in combination. Don't just look at one clue in isolation. How do the clues work together? 'COFFEE-TABLE' and 'REFERENCE' together quickly point to the category of 'BOOKS'.

faqs.question: Why isn't "Journal" the answer?
faqs.answer: While 'Journal' might connect loosely to some clues, it doesn't fit as strongly with 'COFFEE-TABLE' or 'SKETCH' as 'BOOKS' does. The Pinpoint answer needs to create strong, recognizable phrases with all the clues.

faqs.question: What is a coffee table book?
faqs.answer: A coffee table book is a large, visually appealing book that's often placed on a coffee table for decoration and casual browsing. They usually feature photography or art.

faqs.question: How does REFERENCE connect to BOOKS?
faqs.answer: REFERENCE connects to BOOKS because a 'Reference book' is a common type of book used for looking up information, like a dictionary or encyclopedia.
